hints.title: Zero Flipping Allowance Obstacle
hints.text: You may flip at most k zeroes to ones. How can you formulate this as finding the longest contiguous subarray containing at most k zeroes?

hints.title: Dynamic Window Invariant
hints.text: Expand the right boundary. When the count of zeroes in window [left, right] exceeds k, advance left until the zero count returns to at most k.

hints.title: Two-Pointer Expansion Procedure
hints.text: Initialize left = 0, zeroCount = 0, and maxLen = 0. For right in range(len(nums)): if nums[right] == 0, zeroCount += 1. While zeroCount > k: if nums[left] == 0, zeroCount -= 1; left += 1. Update maxLen = max(maxLen, right - left + 1). Return maxLen.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
k: allowed zero flips (0 <= k <= N)
complexity.notes: Dynamic sliding window where both pointers advance at most N times in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating every possible subarray takes O(N^2) which exceeds the 1-second time limit for N = 10^5.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining why both left and right pointers only move forward, guaranteeing amortized O(N) runtime.
